verdict.rationale: Jev is a typed-decision model API, and such a product could plausibly offer versioned, reviewable, revertible saved question or automation definitions, so the axis applies. The evidence only documents model-version pinning and aliases (jev-latest vs. jev-1.13.0). That is an adjacent control over which model answers, not versioning, review, or rollback of the user's own automations. Questions live in user code, so any versioning there is a user-side workaround that earns no credit.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can version, review, and roll back my automations
